q: Does the RC error-suppression exponent (paper ~2.73, this work exact ~2.26) hold for non-Pauli coherent noise models, e.g., amplitude-damping-like non-unitary Kraus operators or correlated ZZ crosstalk between neighboring qubits?
basis: Theorem 1 in the paper strictly requires all-Hermitian Kraus operators. Pauli twirling turns single-qubit unitary Z-rotation noise into a stochastic Pauli channel, but non-unitary noise (T1 decay) or non-local coherent errors are only partially symmetrized. Our replication only tested single-qubit R_Z(epsilon), the easiest case.
next_steps: Reimplement the twirled channel calculation with a per-cycle noise model that mixes R_Z(epsilon) with an amplitude-damping Kraus pair of strength gamma, then fit the RC error vs (epsilon, gamma). Compare against a two-qubit ZZ(alpha) coherent-crosstalk noise model twirled by 2-qubit Pauli group. Predict: RC exponent drops from ~2.3 toward 1 as the non-Hermitian noise fraction grows.

q: How does RC compose with dynamical decoupling (DD) sequences on top of the same QPE circuit? Is the combined suppression additive, multiplicative, or does one interfere with the other?
basis: DD suppresses low-frequency coherent noise via pulse-level echoes; RC suppresses per-cycle coherent noise via logical Pauli twirls. Both target coherent errors but at different timescales, and both consume gate budget. The paper does not combine them.
next_steps: Add XY4 or CPMG DD blocks inside each iterative-PE cycle of our qiskit-aer harness, then repeat the exact-superoperator calculation as a function of (epsilon, DD-period, N_r). Metric: RC-only slope vs DD-only slope vs combined slope on the same coherent-noise sweep. Free endpoint: run on the local qiskit-aer statevector, no hardware.

q: Does the RC exponent match ~2.7 for phase-estimation of a specific chemistry ground-state (e.g., H2 or LiH) unitary, where the underlying phase carries chemical meaning and the eigenphase clusters can be near-degenerate?
basis: The paper's Fig. 3 uses a synthetic 10-qubit Floquet unitary; the Shor demo (Fig. 4) is number-theoretic. Chemistry ground-state phases are the highest-leverage QPE application but have near-degenerate eigenvalues that may interact with RC's stochastic residual differently.
next_steps: Build the H2/STO-3G qubit Hamiltonian in qiskit-nature (Bravyi-Kitaev), Trotterize e^{-iHt}, run bare iterative-PE + RC on the ground-state overlap, fit the error exponent under coherent Trotter noise. Compare with the Floquet result. Free endpoint: local qiskit-aer, small basis.

q: What is the true hardware-runtime overhead of RC on IBM/IonQ hardware for QPE, once compiler-side twirl injection and per-shot recompilation are counted? Does the RC advantage survive the extra latency and calibration drift at fixed wall-clock budget?
basis: Our replication is simulator-only. In practice, RC requires N_r distinct compiled circuits per depth L; each recompile hits the transpiler, calibration cache, and pulse-schedule build. If a hardware backend caches N_r=100 twirled variants per (L, epsilon) point, the per-shot cost may be dominated by compilation, not gate time. The paper does not benchmark this.
next_steps: Run the same iterative-PE + RC harness on a free IBM Q Experience open-plan backend (e.g., ibm_brisbane) with N_r in {1, 10, 100}, fixed total shot budget T. Measure wall-clock per fit point and compare (bare-error at total-shots T) vs (RC-error at total-shots T/N_r) --- the fair comparison. Predict: RC advantage shrinks at small T where compile-time dominates.

q: Is there an adaptive shot-allocation scheme that outperforms uniform N_r-per-depth by concentrating twirl realizations at the depths L where the RC bias residual is largest?
basis: The residual RC error scales as 1/sqrt(N_s * N_r) plus a super-linear coherent-bias term epsilon^k. At small L the bias is negligible and shots are wasted; at large L the aliasing of the ideal cos(2 phi L) signal makes even small residuals dominate. Uniform (N_s, N_r) across L is provably suboptimal.
next_steps: Formulate an information-theoretic cost function C(L, N_s, N_r; epsilon) = variance of phi_hat given the Aer-sampled likelihood, minimize under a total shot budget sum_L N_s(L) * N_r(L) = T. Compare a Cramer-Rao-optimal allocation against uniform on the exact-channel sweep. Metric: phi-error at fixed T. Free endpoint: local optimization, no simulator changes.
